args: In mruby/mrbgems/mruby-proc-binding/src/proc-binding.c, what is the correct project-idiomatic way to keep the mrb_value returned by mrb_proc_source_location() alive while storing it with mrb_iv_set() in mrb_proc_binding()? Specifically, should it be assigned to a local and passed to mrb_gc_protect before mrb_iv_set, and is any arena save/restore required inside this Ruby C method?

The reported ASan failure is a heap-use-after-free in mrb_gc_mark while traversing the live Binding object's IV table. At proc-binding.c line 32, mrb_proc_binding currently calls mrb_iv_set(mrb, binding, MRB_SYM(source_location), mrb_proc_source_location(...)) directly. mrb_proc_source_location creates an array [filename, line] through mrb_assoc_new when location metadata exists. Under incremental/generational sweeping, that newly allocated array can be swept despite its pointer being installed in @source_location, apparently because it was never explicitly rooted/protected across the store. The proposed root-cause fix is to split the expression into a local mrb_value source_location, call mrb_gc_protect(mrb, source_location), and then call mrb_iv_set. I am checking API and arena conventions before making this minimal source change.
